title: EdGeo: A Physics-guided Generative AI Toolkit for Geophysical Monitoring on Edge Devices
problem: Full-waveform inversion for geophysical subsurface exploration using machine learning is severely limited by the scarcity of unprivileged training data. Model pruning, essential for edge deployment, further exacerbates this data limitation and degrades model performance.
motivation: Efficient geophysical subsurface monitoring on edge devices enables real-time velocity mapping for exploration with minimal computational overhead.
method: EdGeo uses a physics-guided diffusion model—a machine learning technique that creates new data by learning from seismic physics equations—to generate detailed maps showing how fast seismic waves travel through rock. It then applies the acoustic wave equation, the physics law governing how earthquakes and seismic waves propagate through the earth, to simulate realistic seismic signals from those maps. These synthetic signals train smaller machine learning models that have been pruned—parts removed to make them small enough to run on edge devices—restoring the accuracy lost during that compression.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using physics-guided machine learning to generate synthetic earthquake signals, which both restores accuracy lost when shrinking models for edge devices and compensates for the scarcity of available training data.
contributions: Physics-guided diffusion-based toolkit for generating high-fidelity synthetic velocity maps
Acoustic wave equation-based synthetic seismic waveform generation for realistic data synthesis
Fine-tuning strategy for recovering pruned model performance using synthetic data
Improved representation of underrepresented geophysical features compared to existing methods
limitations: Limitations not discussed in the provided abstract.
primary_theme: Physics-guided generative AI for edge geophysics
